producer_report.summary:
The squash chain is now built from landed jobs only. A rejected job whose records ship in the squash is no longer a link, so its landed retry no longer looks like a fork.

In `invariant.rs`:
- `closing_jobs` now takes `git` and `change` and returns a `Result`. It drops any job whose recorded `outcome.json` or `outcome-landed.json` in the commit tree exists and none is landed. A job with no outcome record stays in the set, so the per-job check still refuses it. A doc comment says why.
- `chain_problem` lets a chain head name a previous job outside the chain when that job's recorded outcome is not landed. Two other cases are still refused as 'not linked': a previous job that is absent, and one with no outcome record. The head's base must still equal the parent's content.

Tests in `landing_tests.rs`:
- New: a rejected job A, its landed retry B (previous_job = A) and a landed job C following B is accepted, and only B and C are reported as landed.
- New: two landed retries of the same rejected job are refused with 'both follow', and a fork of landed jobs is refused with 'both follow'.
- Changed: in `every_per_job_check_refuses_a_chain_when_a_middle_job_fails_it`, the blocked-outcome case now describes a job that is deliberately outside the chain, so I replaced it with a middle job that has no outcome record. That case is still refused with 'a landing commit adds'.

Docs: decision D74 in `docs/decisions.md`, a bullet in §4.6 of `docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md`, and a CHANGELOG entry."

checks_run.note: Full workspace `cargo test --locked` passed earlier, before a test-only clippy fix. Gate and policy tests re-run after the fix and pass.

open_issues: A squash holding only a rejected job no longer gets a per-job reason from the landing check. It now falls through to the generic 'governed content changed without a verified landing' message (recorded in D74).
Two landed retries of the same rejected job are still refused as 'both follow'. This is intended: they are real forks of landed jobs.
mistakes: First edit left a duplicated brace in closing_jobs, which broke the build. Fixed on the next edit.
First draft of the second new test expected 'both start a chain'. The actual refusal is 'both follow'. I corrected the expectation after the test run.
learnings: closing_jobs had no git access; it now takes git and the change so it can read each job's outcome from the commit tree.

Existing test every_per_job_check_refuses_a_chain_when_a_middle_job_fails_it asserted that a middle job with a Blocked outcome is refused with 'a landing commit adds'. Under the new rule that job is excluded from the chain, so I replaced that case with one where the outcome record is missing.
dyn Fn(usize,&mut Vec<_>) test hooks need closure wrappers if the helper takes a slice (clippy ptr_arg).
